wiki_auszug: Parsing refers to breaking an artifact into its constituent elements and capturing the relationship between those elements. This tag isn't for questions about the self hosted Parse Platform (use the [parse-platform] tag) or parse errors in a particular programming language (use the appropriate language tag instead).
begruendung: G~85% U~15%: Most questions involve regex, ASTs, or algorithmic logic visible in the code/data.

wiki_auszug: Selenium WebDriver provides APIs in different programming languages ("language bindings"). When using this tag, also add a tag for the programming language you are using.
begruendung: G~80% U~20%: Most questions involve coding against the API (selectors, waits, actions), which is visible in the question.

wiki_auszug: A block of arbitrary information, or resource for storing information, accessible by the string-based name or path. Files are available to computer programs and are usually based on some kind of persistent storage.
begruendung: G~80% U~20%: Most questions involve file I/O operations, parsing, or logic visible in the code snippet provided.

wiki_auszug: WinForms is the informal name given to Windows Forms, a GUI class library in the Microsoft .NET Framework and Mono. Questions in this tag should also be tagged with the target framework ([.net] or [mono]) and should ordinarily be tagged with a programming language tag.
begruendung: G~70% U~30%: Most questions involve coding against the WinForms API (controls, events, layout), which is visible in the question.

wiki_auszug: Assembly language questions. Please tag the processor and/or the instruction set you are using, as well as the assembler, a valid set should be like this: ([assembly] [x86] [gnu-assembler] or [att]). Use the [.net-assembly] tag instead for .NET assemblies, [cil] for .NET assembly language, [wasm] for web assembly, and for Java bytecode, use the tag java-bytecode-asm instead.
begruendung: G~80% U~20%: Writing assembly code relies on visible syntax and logic; setup questions are less common than coding questions.

wiki_auszug: GENERAL UBUNTU SUPPORT IS OFF-TOPIC. Support questions may be asked at https://askubuntu.com/. Ubuntu is a free desktop and server operating system based on Debian GNU/Linux. This tag is for programming questions specific to Ubuntu. Do not use it just because you happen to be running Ubuntu
begruendung: G~20% U~80%: Typical questions involve OS configuration, permissions, or environment setup invisible to outsiders.

wiki_auszug: Scikit-learn is a machine-learning library for Python that provides simple and efficient tools for data analysis and data mining, with a focus on machine learning. It is accessible to everybody and reusable in various contexts. It is built on NumPy and SciPy. The project is open source and commercially usable (BSD license).
begruendung: G~85% U~15%: Most questions involve using the library's API, algorithms, or data processing logic visible in the code.

wiki_auszug: Keras is a neural network library providing a high-level API in Python and R. Use this tag for questions relating to how to use this API. Please also include the tag for the language/backend ([python], [r], [tensorflow], [theano], [cntk]) that you are using. If you are using tensorflow's built-in keras, use the [tf.keras] tag.
begruendung: language rule: not a general-purpose language; G share is high as it covers API usage and model logic.

wiki_auszug: The user-facing part of an application. In a desktop application, this would include the windowing framework and the forms the user interacts with; in a command line program it would be the available commands and arguments; and in a web app, it would refer to the HTML and JavaScript.
begruendung: G~80% U~20%: Questions focus on UI logic, DOM manipulation, and framework usage visible in code snippets.

wiki_auszug: Data types for "pointing" at other values: A pointer's value is a memory address where the pointed-to value is stored. This tag should be used for questions involving the use of pointers, not references. Common programming languages using pointers are C, C++, Go, and assembly and intermediate-representation languages; use a specific language tag. Other helpful tags should describe what is being pointed-to (e.g. a function, a struct etc.)
begruendung: G~90% U~10%: Questions involve memory management logic and pointer arithmetic visible in code snippets.

wiki_auszug: SQLAlchemy is a Python SQL toolkit and Object Relational Mapper that gives application developers the full power and flexibility of SQL.
begruendung: language rule: not a pure language tag; G share ~80% (code/API usage) vs U share ~20% (setup/config).

wiki_auszug: An exception is an unusual condition that requires deviation from the program's normal flow. Normally, an exception should not result in total failure, but instead be attended by an exception handler. Exception handling is a built-in construct in many programming languages. Usually, exceptions are handled by unwinding the stack, thus rolling back to a defined state outside the exception's scope, and then invoking a handler block or routine.
begruendung: G~90% U~10%: Exception handling logic is language-specific and visible in code; setup questions are rare.

wiki_auszug: Questions about Angular (not to be confused with AngularJS), the web framework from Google. Use this tag for Angular questions which are not specific to an individual version. For the older AngularJS (1.x) web framework, use the AngularJS tag.
begruendung: language rule: Not a language; G share is high as most issues involve API usage and component logic visible in code.

wiki_auszug: Recursion is a kind of function call in which a function calls itself. Such functions are also called recursive functions. Structural recursion is a method of problem solving where the solution to a problem depends on solutions to smaller instances of the same problem.
begruendung: language rule: not a specific language; G~90% U~10%: recursion logic and base cases are visible in code examples.

wiki_auszug: The graphical representation of a mathematical function or a set of data. There are different kinds of plots, such as line plots, bar plots, or scatter plots.
begruendung: G~80% U~20%: Most questions involve specific plotting libraries (matplotlib, ggplot) where the solution derives from code/data provided.

wiki_auszug: The ASP.NET MVC Framework is an open source web application framework and tooling that implements a version of the model-view-controller (MVC) pattern tailored towards web applications and built upon an ASP.NET technology foundation.
begruendung: G~80% U~20%: Most questions involve code logic, routing, or framework usage visible in the question.

wiki_auszug: Blazor lets you build interactive web UIs using C# instead of JavaScript. It is a feature of ASP.NET Core, the web development framework from Microsoft that extends the .NET developer platform.
begruendung: G~70% U~30%: Most questions involve writing code against the Blazor API (syntax, logic, components), which is visible in the question.

wiki_auszug: React is a JavaScript library for building user interfaces. It uses a declarative, component-based paradigm and aims to be efficient and flexible.
begruendung: language rule: not a whole language; G~85% U~15%: typical questions involve component logic, state management, and API usage visible in the code.

wiki_auszug: Cypress an all-in-one web testing framework and assertion library developed in JavaScript, complete with automatic waits, request mocking, and request stubbing.
begruendung: language rule: not a general-purpose language; G~80% U~20%: typical questions involve writing test code, selectors, and assertions visible in the question.

wiki_auszug:
For questions about Microsoft's .NET application development framework that are specific to version 6.0+ of the framework.
Use only If your question are version-specific
begruendung: language rule: tag contains a specific version number (6.0), which typically implies environment-specific issues like installation, configuration, or platform compatibility.

wiki_auszug: Deep Learning is an area of machine learning whose goal is to learn complex functions using special neural network architectures that are "deep"  (consist of many layers). This tag should be used for questions about implementation of deep learning architectures. General machine learning questions should be tagged "machine learning". Including a tag for the relevant software library (e.g., "keras", "tensorflow","pytorch","fast.ai" etc) is helpful.
begruendung: G~80% U~20%: Most questions involve implementing architectures or debugging code, which relies on visible logic rather than hidden environment details.

wiki_auszug: Indexing data structures is a general technique to improve the speed of data lookups.
begruendung: G~85% U~15%: Typical questions involve implementing or optimizing search structures (hash maps, B-trees) using standard algorithms.

DO NOT USE FOR THE AWS SERVICE (use [aws-lambda] for those questions!) 

Lambdas are anonymous functions or closures in programming languages such as Lisp, C#, C++, Lua, Python, Ruby, JavaScript, Java, Excel or Google sheets. (Also, lambda expression.)
begruendung: language rule: not a single language; estimate G~90% U~10% as questions are about syntax/logic of anonymous functions.

wiki_auszug: Nest (NestJS) is a framework for building efficient, scalable Node.js server-side applications. It uses progressive JavaScript, is built with and fully supports TypeScript.
begruendung: G~80% U~20%: Most questions involve code logic, decorators, or API usage visible in the question.

wiki_auszug: CSS (Cascading Style Sheets) is a representation style sheet language used for describing the look and formatting of HTML (HyperText Markup Language), XML (Extensible Markup Language) documents and SVG elements including (but not limited to) colors, layout, fonts, and animations. It also describes how elements should be rendered on screen, on paper, in speech, or on other media.
begruendung: language rule: css is a style sheet language; solutions derive from code/logic visible in the question.

wiki_auszug: Sorting is the process of applying some order to a collection of items.
begruendung: language rule: not a specific language; G~90% U~10%: sorting logic and algorithms are visible in code/data questions.

wiki_auszug: Use this tag for questions specific to version 3 of Vue.js, an open-source, progressive Javascript framework for building user interfaces.
begruendung: language rule: not a general-purpose language; estimate G~85% U~15%: most questions involve code usage, syntax, and API logic visible in the question.

wiki_auszug: A template for creating new objects that describes the common state(s) and behavior(s). NOT TO BE CONFUSED WITH HTML CLASSES OR CSS CLASS SELECTORS. Use [html] or [css] instead.
begruendung: language rule: not a language; G~85% U~15%: questions about class definitions, inheritance, and object instantiation are solvable from code alone.

wiki_auszug: A DateTime object in many programming languages describes a date and a time of day.  It can express either an instant in time or a position on a calendar, depending on the context in which it is used and the specific implementation.  This tag can be used for all date and time related issues.
begruendung: G~85% U~15%: Most questions involve parsing, formatting, or calculating with dates using standard library APIs.

wiki_auszug:
JSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is a serializable data interchange format that is a machine and human readable. 

Do not use this tag for native JavaScript objects or JavaScript object literals. 

Before you ask a question, validate your JSON using a JSON validator such as JSONLint (https://jsonlint.com).
begruendung: language rule: JSON is a data format, not a programming language; typical questions involve parsing, validation, or syntax errors visible in the question.

wiki_auszug: The primary purpose of XPath is to address parts of an XML document. It also provides basic facilities for manipulation of strings, numbers and booleans. XPath uses a compact, non-XML syntax. XPath operates on the abstract, logical structure of an XML document, rather than its surface syntax.
begruendung: G~90% U~10%: Query logic and pattern matching are visible in questions; setup is rare.

wiki_auszug: HTML (HyperText Markup Language) is the markup language for creating web pages and other information to be displayed in a web browser. Questions regarding HTML should include a minimal reproducible example and some idea of what you're trying to achieve. This tag is rarely used alone and is often paired with CSS and JavaScript.
begruendung: language rule: html is a general-purpose markup language; solutions derive from code/logic visible in the question.

wiki_auszug: Firebase Authentication provides backend services, easy-to-use SDKs, and ready-made UI libraries to authenticate users to your app.
begruendung: G~70% U~30%: Most questions involve API usage, token handling, or logic errors visible in code snippets.

wiki_auszug: Ruby on Rails is an open source full-stack web application framework written in Ruby. It follows the popular MVC framework model and is known for its "convention over configuration" approach to application development.
begruendung: language rule: not a pure language; estimate G~80% U~20% as most questions involve code logic, API usage, or MVC patterns visible in the question.

begruendung: G~80% U~20%: Most questions involve implementing algorithms or debugging code visible in the post.

wiki_auszug: Beautiful Soup is a Python package for parsing HTML/XML. The latest version of this package is version 4, imported as bs4.
begruendung: language rule: not a general-purpose language; G~85% U~15%: typical questions involve parsing logic and API usage visible in the code.

wiki_auszug: Google Cloud Platform provides cloud computing services that let you build applications and websites, store data, and analyze data on Google's infrastructure.
begruendung: G~30% U~70%: Typical questions involve installation, configuration, permissions, or specific GCP service setup not visible in the question text.

wiki_auszug: Apache Spark is an open source distributed data processing engine written in Scala providing a unified API and distributed data sets to users for both batch and streaming processing. Use cases for Apache Spark often are related to machine/deep learning and graph processing.
begruendung: G~80% U~20%: Most questions involve code, API usage, or data processing logic visible in the question.

wiki_auszug: 'discord.py' is a Python 3.8+ library for interfacing with the official Discord API. This tag should only be used when referring to the discord.py library. If using the [nextcord] or [pycord] fork, please use these tags instead if the question refers to them specifically; otherwise, please use both the fork's tag and [discord.py]. Please check if all necessary intents are enabled in the code and your Discord Developer Portal.
begruendung: G~85% U~15%: Most questions involve API usage, intent configuration in code, or error handling visible in snippets.
